clue.text: Light diversion forcing father into response

indicators.note: forcing something into another thing pushes it inside, so one piece goes within the other
into tells us where the forced piece ends up: within the word for response

parts.note: a response is a reaction
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A father is pushed into giving some reply, with a bit of playful light distraction thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light diversion' reads like a pleasant distraction, but it is the bending of light rays.
explanation.definitionFit: The bending of a light ray as it passes from one medium to another is its physical diversion from a straight path.

clue.text: Rank old car with the top off

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Someone grades an old convertible car that has its roof down.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank something is to grade or assess it, the same verb sense as rate.

clue.text: Outburst and terrible earful over parking

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next one
terrible suggests the word earful is mangled into a new order

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and gives a dreadful telling-off about a parking matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles EARFUL into FLAREU; 'parking' looks like the subject of the row but only supplies its road-sign letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden eruption of anger or violence is called a flare-up, an idiom for a burst of trouble.

clue.text: Unfortunately adopted by European from a Pacific region

indicators.note: being adopted by someone means being taken in, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an Austrian is a European from Austria
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Sadly, a child from somewhere in the Pacific is adopted by a European family.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone or something belonging to Australia, New Zealand and nearby islands of the South Pacific.

clue.text: Cost associated with football sticker

definitions.meaning: in football, a club pays a fee to buy a player from another club, the move being named after that deal
a decal design that is pressed on to a surface from backing paper

explanation.surface: A football sticker, the kind collected in albums, and what it costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A player's move between clubs and its fee carry the word; it is also a picture applied by pressing, a sticker.

clue.text: Old church has brief solution for a large amount

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word for solution loses its ending

parts.note: the solution to a puzzle is its answer

explanation.surface: An old church has a short answer ready for some big total.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, oceans of something means a vast quantity, like lots or heaps.

clue.text: Fare available for soldiers out without protection?

parts.note: soldiers are men, the ranks as opposed to officers

indicators.note: the outer letters protect the word like a casing; take them away and only the centre of out remains

explanation.surface: Soldiers out in the field with no cover wonder what food is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out without protection' is out stripped of its outside letters, leaving U.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's list sets out the dishes, the fare, that can be ordered.

clue.text: Ring on this gong to support member of the Lords?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: an earl is a peer who may sit in the House of Lords
gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A peer hoping a medal will boost his standing in the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' is an earring, worn on this soft part of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earrings are commonly worn through the soft lower lobe of the ear, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: Inverted and sad after leading team

indicators.note: after puts the word for sad following the other pieces

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, leading
a side is a team in sport
down means sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A team that was ahead turns things on their head and ends up gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned over so its top is at the bottom is inverted.

clue.text: Converted coach without one must get criticised

indicators.note: without here means losing a letter, so the word for one is dropped

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, part of a train
I is the Roman numeral for one
slated is British informal for harshly criticised

explanation.surface: A sports coach who is short one player gets criticised for the change.
explanation.definitionFit: Text rendered into another language has been converted, the sense of translated as changed in form.

clue.text: British Standard applied to Golden Globes

indicators.note: applied to means the first-named piece is attached after the word that follows it

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard

explanation.surface: A quality mark is stamped on the Golden Globe awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres or globes are orbs, as in the royal orb carried at coronations.

clue.text: Fatter, possibly eating whilst getting second opinion

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
possibly signals that the letters of fatter could be arranged another way

parts.note: though and whilst can both mean although

explanation.surface: Someone getting fatter keeps eating and has doubts about it later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes AFTERT from the fatter fodder, and 'eating' swallows the word for whilst before the final T; 'second opinion' means a later thought, not a doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: A later idea added after first reflection is like a second view on the matter.

clue.text: Raise tail

definitions.meaning: to bring up children or lift something, a verb
the back end or bottom, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to bring up or lift and the hindmost part, the backside.

clue.text: Cool girl fans do badly with no end of potential

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of the fodder are jumbled
with no means some letters of the fodder are left out of the rearrangement
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A calm young woman whose admirers perform poorly and fail to reach their potential.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GIRL FANS DO, drop L (the end of potential), and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and calmness under pressure is coolness, the French borrowing meaning literally cold blood.

clue.text: Restraint of newspapers in region with no golf

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
with no means the given letter is taken out

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Newspapers in a region with no golf course feel held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' strips G from region to leave REION, and 'in' sets the newspapers inside it; golf is G by the phonetic alphabet, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back or suppressing feelings or people is a form of restraint.

clue.text: Error to turn right — next to that is where plants are trained

indicators.note: to turn means the word for error is read backwards

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A mistake about turning right, next to the place where plants are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees and shrubs are trained flat against a wall or a lattice frame of this kind.

clue.text: Inscription, say, included in loan

indicators.note: being included in something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a lend is informal British for a loan
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: An inscription, for instance, forms part of a loan agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The words on a coin, medal or below a picture are its inscription or caption.

clue.text: Hypocrite pairs off outside hotel on the borders of Europe

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
off implies the letters of pairs are out of place and need rearranging

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A two-faced person sends couples off from a hotel at Europe's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIRS jumbled into PARIS goes outside H, giving PHARIS, then EE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were criticised in the Gospels as sanctimonious, so the name became a byword for a sanctimonious fraud.

clue.text: Part of salad plate given to artist

indicators.note: given to means the plate is handed on, placed after the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: An artist is handed a plate holding some salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This crunchy red root vegetable is commonly sliced into a salad.

clue.text: Hung over?

parts.note: looks like suffering after drinking, but means suspended loosely over something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hung over' suggests a headache after drinking; read literally, it is hanging over the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left swinging loosely from above has been suspended, hung over an edge.

clue.text: TV programme about bowlers, perhaps, who must develop

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
bowlers are an example of hats

indicators.note: develop suggests the letters of who change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cricket programme about bowlers and who will improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowlers' suggests cricket, but these are bowler hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A television format where a host interviews guests in conversation is this sort of programme.

clue.text: Sanitation of hospital eyeing reforms

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: reforms suggests the letters of eyeing are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital has its eye on reforming its sanitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanliness practices that keep disease away are sanitation in its broad sense.

clue.text: Rumoured seat of power for cast

indicators.note: rumoured suggests something passed by word of mouth, so the word must be heard

parts.note: a throne is the seat of a monarch's power

explanation.surface: Gossip about which seat of power has been cast aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cast has been hurled or tossed, the past participle of throw.

clue.text: Person lying falsifed heat burns

indicators.note: falsified (misprinted in the clue) means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A liar falsely claims the heat has caused burns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person lying' suggests a liar, but this one is lying down in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stretched out in the sun to tan is a person lying down, not telling fibs.

clue.text: Sort of party involved in floor gymnastics?

indicators.note: involved in means the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A party that involves floor exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, debauched gathering is a kind of party.

clue.text: Waste time showing instruction to printer

indicators.note: showing means the letters are on view within the words given

explanation.surface: An instruction to the printer not to waste time.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark meaning let it stand tells the printer to keep a deleted text.

clue.text: Troubles caused by factories starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the word begins one letter in, its first letter dropped

parts.note: mills are factories, such as cotton mills

explanation.surface: Problems arising from factories opening behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments and misfortunes are troubles, the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Visitor judged broadcast by theatre audience

parts.note: the house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: to have guessed is to have judged roughly

explanation.surface: A visitor is assessed by a theatre crowd in a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A person staying for a while in someone's home is a visitor.

clue.text: Signify agreement and finally remove swelling

parts.note: to nod is to signal agreement

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Agreeing at last to have a swelling taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob or lump, as in a lymph gland or on a plant stem, is a swelling.

clue.text: Maybe shares popular garb for the clergy

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vestment is a robe worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Perhaps clerical robes are the fashionable thing to buy shares in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks and shares are examples of something bought for financial return.
